MCP server hand-written; @modelcontextprotocol/sdk rejected as a runtime dependency
why: The needed surface is initialize + tools/list + tools/call + one notification over newline-delimited JSON-RPC — about one file. A dependency would bring a version to track, a supply chain to trust and an install step to a tool whose distribution story is 'clone and run with Node'. The cost is real and named: when the protocol revises, that file is ours. Version is pinned and echoed so a mismatch is visible.

text: atlas ask is a batch query, not a session driver (M-2)
why: MCP cannot drive a session and the Agent SDK is a different product. A general-purpose agent runner inside a documentation tool would be two products in one package. What CI actually wants is one structured answer with an exit code, which needs no agent at all.

A-22's warning cannot fire against a build that predates it
why: The older build never writes the owner record, so the newer one sees itself as last holder and stays silent. Inherent: an old build cannot announce what it does not know about. Works between any two builds carrying the code.

text: a subagent ran git stash on the shared working tree and discarded a journal record
why: Parallel agents share one tree. Stash/pop is not safe there — the pop collided with files the test run had rewritten, and checkout -- discarded a record written seconds earlier. Agents must be told not to stash.
